solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Square bill for bed (4-6)

blocks.note: four is a square number (2 × 2)
a bill is a notice stuck on a wall, a poster

annotation.surface: Someone settles up a straight bill for a bed, perhaps at a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square bill' reads as settling an account; here 'square' is a number, and FOUR is the square of two.
annotation.definitionFit: A four-poster is a bed with a post at each corner, often holding a canopy.

entries.clue: Silly person, most robust and most imprudent (12)

blocks.note: a fool is a silly person
hardiest = toughest, most robust

annotation.surface: A description of someone both very tough and very reckless, the classic daredevil.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces also point at the meaning: the fool who is too hardy to feel fear is exactly the foolhardy one.
annotation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rashly bold, so the foolhardiest is the most imprudent.

entries.clue: Pronounce complete (5)

blocks.note: a verb: to say a word aloud
an adjective: total, as in '___ nonsense'

annotation.surface: Two words that could be an instruction to finish saying something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pronounce complete' reads like a verdict being declared; split it into a verb and an adjective, each meaning UTTER.
annotation.definitionFit: Utter is both a verb (to speak) and an adjective (total, complete).

entries.clue: At first, policeman asked dealer to come quietly (3)

indicatorNotes.At first: take the first letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: first letter of Policeman
first letter of Asked
first letter of Dealer

annotation.surface: A police officer arrests a drug dealer and tells him to come quietly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come quietly' is the arrest cliché, but here it means move softly, the way a cat pads along.
annotation.definitionFit: To pad is to walk with soft, quiet steps.

entries.clue: American soldiers turned up, and not an Italian (6)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning a word up means reading it bottom to top

blocks.note: GIs are US soldiers
nor = and not

annotation.surface: A report that some GIs showed up, but no Italian did.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And not' looks like part of the sentence's grammar but supplies NOR.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the Italian title for Mr, so English uses it for an Italian gentleman.

entries.clue: Light refreshment and teas regularly sustaining teams (9)

indicatorNotes.sustaining: in a down entry, what sustains something props it up from below, so these letters go underneath

blocks.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven
second and fourth letters of tEaS

annotation.surface: Players are kept going by snacks and cups of tea during a match.
annotation.walkthrough: Cricket and football sides have eleven players, so teams are ELEVENS. Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, usually tea or coffee and a biscuit.
annotation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a light snack taken around eleven in the morning.

entries.clue: Balm spread over daughter and a foreign character (6)

indicatorNotes.spread: the letters of BALM are spread out into a new order

blocks.note: anagram of BALM
d = daughter, as in family trees
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: Soothing ointment being applied to a daughter and a foreign person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' sits in front of 'daughter' to say the rearranged BALM comes first in this down entry. 'Character' is a letter, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

entries.clue: Woman’s clear about any number wanting to go with the group (4,8)

annotation.definition: wanting to go with the group

blocks.note: her = the woman's
distinct = clear; it opens as DI and closes as STINCT
n = any number, as in maths

annotation.surface: Talk of a woman who is plainly keen to fit in with everybody else.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is the possessive, so 'woman's' is simply her. The enumeration splits the letters after the D, not where the pieces join.
annotation.definitionFit: Herd instinct is the urge to follow the crowd, a desire to go with the group.

entries.clue: Chose surgical procedure by Edward (5)

blocks.note: op = operation
Ted is a short form of Edward

annotation.surface: Someone has picked a surgical operation to be carried out by a surgeon called Edward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' reads as the surgeon doing the operation; it only means next to, placing the two pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to opt is to choose, and both past tenses match.

entries.clue: Furiously angered, one explodes (7)

indicatorNotes.Furiously: the letters of ANGERED are thrown about wildly

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Somebody driven to fury finally blows up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One explodes' seems to be the angry person losing their temper; it is the thing that literally explodes.
annotation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb, something that explodes.

entries.clue: Stupidly chose poor method of prediction (9)

indicatorNotes.Stupidly: the letters are arranged in a senseless way, to be put right

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone foolishly picked a bad way of forecasting the future.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sceptic's joke: the answer is itself arguably a poor method of prediction.
annotation.definitionFit: A horoscope forecasts a person's future from the stars.

entries.clue: Bombardment fell all over the place in county (9)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: the letters of FELL are scattered
indicatorNotes.in: the scattered letters go inside SHIRE

blocks.note: a shire is an English county; it opens as SH and closes as IRE
anagram of FELL

annotation.surface: Shells rained down everywhere across the county.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's shells land 'all over the place'; that phrase is really scrambling FELL. SH + ELLF + IRE.
annotation.definitionFit: Shellfire is artillery fire, a bombardment with shells.

entries.clue: Unwell, Pat is sent back (3)

blocks.note: to pat is to dab lightly

annotation.surface: A patient named Pat is too ill and gets sent home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name, but it is the verb: a pat is a dab.
annotation.definitionFit: Feeling bad means feeling unwell.

entries.clue: Very common to carry large weapon (5)

indicatorNotes.to carry: RIFE holds the L inside it

blocks.note: rife = widespread, very common; it opens as RIF and closes as E
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: It is normal for people to carry a big gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very common' reads as describing how often people go armed; it is a single adjective for widespread.
annotation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun, a weapon.

entries.clue: Easily angered, hiding new party clothes (6)

indicatorNotes.hiding: FIERY hides the N inside it

blocks.note: a fiery temper is easily angered; it opens as FI and closes as ERY
n = new

annotation.surface: A hot-tempered person is concealing a fresh outfit for a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' feels like secrecy in the surface; it only means the new letter sits inside the hot-tempered word.
annotation.definitionFit: Finery is showy, elegant clothing worn for special occasions such as parties.

entries.clue: Health resort in the country (5)

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A wellness retreat located out in the countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the country' reads as 'rural'; the IN is used as it stands and 'the country' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular country in southern Europe.

entries.clue: Tail used to smoke? (3-3)

blocks.note: the surface reading: the wagging back part of an animal
the meant reading: what is left once a cigarette has been smoked

annotation.surface: A strange question about using a tail for smoking.
annotation.walkthrough: Dog-end is British slang for a cigarette butt, the used end of something smoked. A tail is literally a dog's end, which is the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A dog-end is the stub left after a cigarette has been smoked, something already used for smoking.

entries.clue: Popular name for hotel (3)

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
n = name, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A well-liked name to give a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular name' reads as a favourite choice of name; it is two pieces, 'in' meaning fashionable and N for name.
annotation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering rooms.

entries.clue: Hurry along appearance before market (4,5)

blocks.note: one's looks are one's appearance
a mart is a market

annotation.surface: Someone is rushed through so they can appear before a market, like a trader or an auction lot.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration splits the letters one place earlier than the pieces join. 'Look smart' is a British command meaning get a move on.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Look smart!' means be quick about it, hurry along.

entries.clue: A side creating huge admiration (5)

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a flank: the left or right part of a building, stage or army

annotation.surface: A team is so good it wins huge admiration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A side' suggests a sports team; here 'side' is a flank, as in the east side of a house.
annotation.definitionFit: Awing is filling someone with awe, creating huge admiration.

entries.clue: Court proceedings are initiated by this waiter’s work (7)

annotation.definition: Court proceedings are initiated by this

blocks.clueFragment: Court proceedings are initiated by this
blocks.note: the formal delivery of a writ or summons, which starts a legal action
waiting at table, bringing food and drink to diners

annotation.surface: A waiter's efforts somehow set off a lawsuit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a customer suing over bad service; also note a tennis point, played on a court, begins with a service too.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal proceedings begin with service of the papers, and serving diners is a waiter's work.

entries.clue: Kid, one in outbuilding (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'one in outbuilding' says the one is located inside the building, so its letter goes inside

blocks.note: a barn is a farm outbuilding; it opens as BA and closes as RN
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A young goat, a kid, is inside a barn.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard makes 'kid' a young goat; it is a child. Bairn is Scottish and northern English for a child.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: the Scottish and northern English word for a child, which 'kid' is informally.

entries.clue: Read out letter for social worker? (3)

indicatorNotes.Read out: saying the letter aloud gives the answer's sound

blocks.note: the second letter of the alphabet, said out loud

annotation.surface: A letter is read aloud on behalf of a social worker.
annotation.walkthrough: A social worker seems to be a job in welfare; the question mark flags that a worker bee lives in a social colony.
annotation.definitionFit: Bees are social insects and the workers do the labour of the hive.

entries.clue: Insensitive with rowing team as a heavy encumbrance (4,6)

blocks.note: dead = numb, insensitive
w = with, as in abbreviations like w/
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

annotation.surface: An unfeeling rower is dragging the rest of the crew down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rowing team' is not decoration: in rowing an eight is a boat of eight oarsmen, and the crew itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A dead weight is a heavy, inert load, a burden or encumbrance.
